# Skill: test-driven-development

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

This is an obligation to record the condition. It does not, by itself, assign construction or publication responsibility to Core. Approval is not conformance evidence and does not change Task 17 statuses.

### T18-DEC-02 — `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE`

- Adapter owns Assessment construction using domain-specific identity, provenance and time context.
- Core owns normative semantic validation.
- Core validation MUST be enforced on every supported registration path.
- A standalone validator that callers can bypass is insufficient.
- An old public registration API MUST NOT remain a validation bypass.
- Publication and retention remain separate responsibilities and must be explicitly assigned by the relevant boundary.
- Downstream consumption does not automatically accept the Assessment as truth or grant authority.

The adapter constructs candidates and initiates admission through the Core API; it must not mutate admitted state. Persistent storage is **caller-managed**. Publication and retention remain **OPEN**. # Remediation Roadmap — Task 18

**Audit base:** `2a83c65`. **Planning only.** `T18-DEC-01` and `T18-DEC-02` are approved; no implementation task is executed. `T18-02A` is eligible for planning; its acceptance is blocked on the registration-ownership decision. `T18-02B` is BLOCKED on the C-2 model; `T18-02C` is retired / superseded.

## 1. How to read this roadmap

- `Task priority` is remediation urgency. `Requirement priority` is in `disposition-matrix.md`.
- Conditional tasks are valid only after their decision resolves ownership.
- A task is closed only by the evidence named in its acceptance criteria, not by the existence of a plan.
- Task 18 does not edit `docs/CORE-001.md`; normative amendments go through `T18-SPEC-01`.

## 2. Approved decision outcomes

`T18-01` is complete:

- `T18-DEC-01` = **`REQ-LOCAL`**: local Assessment recording required for `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` and `CYCLE_DETECTED`.
- `T18-DEC-02` = **`OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE`**: adapter constructs; Core validates; registration/publication ownership remains OPEN (see `decision-register.md` §3).

| Status | DEC-01 | DEC-02 | Eligible remediation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Approved** | `REQ-LOCAL` | `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE` | `T18-02A` planning-eligible, acceptance blocked on registration ownership; `T18-02B` blocked on C-2 model; `T18-02C` retired / superseded |
| Alternative (not selected) | `REQ-LOCAL` | `OWN-CORE` | `PATH-A`; not active |
| Alternative (not selected) | `REQ-EXTERNAL` / `REQ-NONE` | n/a | `PATH-C`; `T18-SPEC-01` only |

**Path correction:** `VAL-CORE-CONSTRUCTION` is only compatible with `OWN-CORE`; it is not an adapter option. The selected path is `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE`; see `decision-register.md` §3 for scope and enforcement.

### Assessment Emission Boundary Evidence (AEBE)

AEBE is a shared deliverable, not a task. It requires:

---AEBE---

1. An Assessment produced from graph state with the exact claim: `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` for an orphan, `CYCLE_DETECTED` for a cycle.
2. Negative evidence: a resolved parent produces no `PARENT_UNRESOLVED`; an acyclic graph produces no `CYCLE_DETECTED`.
3. Ownership: the assessment is frozen/registered by the assigned registration boundary; the graph and descriptor are unchanged. Registration ownership is currently OPEN.
4. Boundary authenticity: the evidence comes from the boundary that actually owns emission. A hand-constructed literal in a test is not AEBE.
5. Validation: see `decision-register.md` §3; AEBE must show enforcement and malformed rejection.
6. Public API: the evidence uses the package root; an internal-module import is an API boundary gap.

T18-13 depends on AEBE, not on a specific implementation task.

## 3. Task table

# CORE-001 Conformance Gap Disposition — Task 18

**Status:** Planning and disposition artifact. Two decisions approved (`T18-DEC-01`, `T18-DEC-02`); all others OPEN. No remediation implemented.
**Audit base:** commit `2a83c65` (`main`, Task 17 merged).
**Normative source:** `docs/CORE-001.md`, UIA-CORE-001 Rev 0.3.3.

**Task 18 artifacts:** this README, `disposition-matrix.md`, `remediation-roadmap.md`, `decision-register.md`, `reconciliation-notes.md`.

## 1. Purpose and scope

Task 17 established what the implementation proves, what it does not, and what remains normatively blocked. Task 18 answers the next question: for each of the 23 non-PASS items, what is missing, what kind of gap is it, what is the smallest valid next step, what must precede it, and what evidence would justify a status change?

---4.1---
| P3 | 12 | N-004, N-020, N-026, N-079, N-084, N-140, N-145, N-156, N-169, N-170, N-174, N-175 |
| **Total** | **23** | |

### 4.1 Approved decisions

- **T18-DEC-01 — `REQ-LOCAL`:** CORE-001 requires a local Assessment recording `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` and `CYCLE_DETECTED`. This is a recording obligation; it does not assign construction/publication to Core.
- **T18-DEC-02 — `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE`:** adapter constructs the Assessment; Core owns semantic validation. Registration/publication/retention ownership remains OPEN; `T18-02A` is planning-eligible but cannot be accepted until registration ownership is assigned. See `decision-register.md` §3 for the canonical scope and enforcement.

Still OPEN: C-2 subject model, exact Assessment shape/provenance, publication/retention ownership, and C-2.a3 / CORE-003.

## 5. Roadmap overview

| Task | Type | Priority | Risk scope |
---5---
| Task | Type | Priority | Risk scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T18-01 Assessment-emission decision package | specification/design | P1 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-02A C-1 adapter emission (planning-eligible; acceptance blocked on registration ownership) | implementation + tests | P1 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-02B C-2.a2 adapter emission (blocked on C-2 model) | implementation + tests | P1 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |

| T18-05 Digest verification (conditional) | decision + implementation/test or docs | P3 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-06 Signed-at trust precondition | specification decision + docs | P2 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-07 Runtime execution limitation | documentation-only | P3 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-08 Contested-claim gating boundary | cross-spec decision/docs | P3 | `AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY` |
| T18-09A Assurance ambiguity decisions | specification decisions | P1 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-09B CONTENT_HASH decision | specification decision | P3 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-09C Trusted-time decision | specification decision | P2 | `EXTERNAL_READINESS` |
| T18-09D N-172 readiness evidence decision | specification decision | P2 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-10 Cross-spec packages | cross-spec integration | P3 | `CROSS_SPEC` |
| T18-11 External readiness | external dependency | P3 | `EXTERNAL_READINESS` |
| T18-12 Documentation reconciliation | documentation-only | P3 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |
| T18-13 Readiness closure evidence | readiness/test | P1 | `EXTERNAL_READINESS` |
| T18-SPEC-01 Specification-change package (conditional) | specification | P2 | `CORE-001_RUNTIME` |

Milestones:
---LIMITS---
Recorded in `reconciliation-notes.md`; Task 17 files are untouched.

2. `N-140` is a MAY requirement marked NOT COVERED; absence of a MAY capability is an intentional limitation, not a conformance gap.
3. `N-026` is a CORE-002 boundary requirement marked PARTIAL in a CORE-001 audit; it is a boundary, not a CORE-001 runtime defect.

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |

| `disposition-matrix.md` | 23 rows with disposition, risk scope, priority, dependencies, closure evidence |
| `remediation-roadmap.md` | Tasks, dependency graph, milestones, critical path, acceptance criteria |
| `decision-register.md` | `T18-DEC-01…14`; 2 APPROVED, 12 OPEN |
| `reconciliation-notes.md` | `T18-DEC-01`/`T18-DEC-02` approval, PATH-B correction, N-169 erratum, N-140 reclassification proposal, traceability gaps |

- Only `T18-DEC-01` and `T18-DEC-02` are approved; all other decisions remain OPEN.
- No remediation task is implemented.
- No Task 17 status is changed.
- No CORE-001 normative text is amended.

content.text:
```ts
function assessEdge(
  edgeRef: EdgeRef,
  candidateAssessments: readonly ContinuityAssessment[],
  policy: Policy,
  ctx: TemporalContext,
): Result<ApplicableAssessments>;

function evaluateAssurance(
  applicable: ApplicableAssessments,
  requirement: ContinuityAssuranceRequirement,
  policy: Policy,
  ctx: TemporalContext,
): AssuranceResult;

function registerAssessment(
  existing: readonly DeepReadonly<ContinuityAssessment>[],
  successor: ContinuityAssessment,
): Result<readonly DeepReadonly<ContinuityAssessment>[]>;
```

**Semantics**

- `assessEdge` is the sole constructor of `ApplicableAssessments`. It deep-copies the candidates, rejects duplicate `assessment_id` values with `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`, freezes a fresh `EdgeRef`, and filters by the triple `subject_version_id === edge.child`, `declared_relation === edge.relation`, `edge.parent ∈ parent_version_ids`. One assessment with several parents can therefore apply to several merge edges.
- The applicable set is sorted by `assessment_id` before the policy hook and again before storage. `unresolved` is `true` exactly when the final set is empty.
- The policy hook may only narrow. Items are matched back by `assessment_id` against the core copy, so a hook cannot inject altered claims under a known id, and duplicates are dropped. Discarded items are not exposed in the public type and are never consumed by assurance evaluation.
- The stored `edge` is the same frozen object passed to the hook, so a hook cannot rebind the edge.
- The result is branded with a module-private symbol via `Object.defineProperty` (non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable), frozen, and registered in a module-private `WeakSet`.
- `evaluateAssurance` first checks `WeakSet` membership. An unbranded value — including a structurally identical object, a forged string property or an object inheriting a branded one — returns `MechanismFailure { code: 'E_APPLICABLE_ASSESSMENTS_UNBRANDED' }` before any assurance logic runs.
- Trusted assessors resolve as `requirement.trusted_assessors ?? policy.trustedAssessorDefault ?? []`. There is no trust-all default; an empty list means no assessment is trusted.
- Only trusted assessments contribute verified claims. If `policy.conflictPredicate` is defined and fires for any pair, the result is `CONTESTED`; this check runs before the missing/disallowed computation. By default the predicate is `undefined`, so `CONTESTED` is unreachable.
- `missing` is the sorted set of required claims absent from the union of verified claims; `disallowed` is the sorted set of verified claims listed in `disallowed_claims`. Either non-empty yields `UNSATISFIED` with `ERR_ASSURANCE_PREDICATE_UNSATISFIED` and the fixed `note`. No negative finding about a claim is established.
- `unverified_claims` is not read by assurance evaluation at all: it neither supports nor refutes a required claim. Only `verified_claims` count.
- `registerAssessment` is copy-on-write. A self-supersession or a supersession chain that would cycle returns `CYCLE_DETECTED`; a duplicate `assessment_id` or unknown `supersedes_assessment_id` returns `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`. Existing records are copied and frozen, never mutated.
- Supersession does not remove the predecessor from applicability and there is no "latest wins" rule. Choosing between a predecessor and its successor is left to `Policy.applicableAssessments`.

**Failure modes:** `E_APPLICABLE_ASSESSMENTS_UNBRANDED`, `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`, `E_OWNERSHIP_UNSUPPORTED`, `CYCLE_DETECTED`, and the `UNSATISFIED`/`CONTESTED` values above.

**Normative source:** §6.2–§6.4, §8.5. Branding, id-based hook narrowing, sort order and supersession mechanics are `ID-T08`. `CONTESTED` detection is **A-4b BLOCKED**.

+### 2.12a `adapters/orphan-assessment.ts` (experimental reference)
+
+**Responsibility:** C-1 orphan Assessment construction. This is an experimental reference adapter API, not a CORE-001 protocol API; it carries no stability guarantee or compatibility commitment.
+
+```ts
+interface OrphanAssessmentRequest {
+  readonly graph: LineageGraph;
+  readonly child: IdentityVersionID;
+  readonly existing: readonly DeepReadonly<ContinuityAssessment>[];
+  readonly assessmentIdFor: (
+    relation: LineageRelationType,
+    parents: readonly IdentityVersionID[],
+  ) => AssessmentID;
+  readonly assessment_profile_ref: string;
+  readonly assessment_method_version: string;
+  readonly assessed_by: DomainID;
+  readonly assessed_at: Timestamp;
+  readonly evidence_refs?: readonly string[];
+}
+
+function emitOrphanAssessment(
+  request: OrphanAssessmentRequest,
+): Result<OrphanAssessmentEmission>;
+```
+
+**Semantics**
+
+- The adapter groups `graph.edges` by `(child, relation)` for the requested child, includes the complete declared parent set for each group, and emits only groups with at least one parent absent from `graph.nodes`.
+- `assessmentIdFor` is called once per emitted group, in sorted relation order and sorted parent order. The adapter validates the returned ID as a non-empty string. It does not generate IDs.
+- The adapter calls `registerOrphanAssessments` once for the complete batch. It stops before Core admission if the graph is not builder-issued, the child is absent, the callback throws, or an ID is invalid.
+- The returned `assessments` are the admitted tail of the frozen registered representation; `registered` is the complete frozen representation.
+- `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` is declaration-scoped. Applicability of the Assessment to a resolved edge does not make that edge unresolved.
+- Callback side effects are outside Core atomicity and are not rolled back. Caller persistence occurs only after successful admission.
+
 ### 2.13 `core/traversal.ts`
 
 **Responsibility:** §8 conditional version binding in three independently callable phases, plus orchestration. The phase contracts are in §3; this section lists the API.

# AEBE — C-1 Orphan Assessment

**Task:** T18-02A.
**Scope:** C-1 / N-138 / `CASE-C-1.a3` only.
**Status:** Implementation evidence recorded. This is not a Task 17 status change and does not resolve `T18-DEC-15`.

## 1. What this evidence establishes

| Claim | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| The assessment is constructed by the adapter boundary, not a hand-built test literal | `tests/unit/orphan-assessment.test.ts` and `tests/conformance/c.test.ts` call `emitOrphanAssessment` from the package root |
| Core validates the candidate generically and contextually | `tests/unit/assessment-validation.test.ts`; the adapter path calls `registerOrphanAssessments` |
| Core owns admission and returns an immutable representation | `tests/unit/assessment-validation.test.ts` batch cases; `Object.isFrozen` assertions |
| The exact C-1 claim is recorded | `unverified_claims` equals `['PARENT_UNRESOLVED']` in the positive and mixed-parent cases |
| A resolved parent produces no C-1 assessment | `C-1 resolved parent produces no PARENT_UNRESOLVED Assessment` |
| `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` is declaration-scoped, not edge-scoped | `assessEdge returns the same assessment for resolved and unresolved edges` |
| The graph and descriptor inputs are not mutated | JSON snapshots before/after; graph deep-freeze tests |
| Generic registration cannot admit a C-1 claim | `rejects PARENT_UNRESOLVED from generic registration` |
| Batch admission is all-or-none | batch cases in `tests/unit/assessment-validation.test.ts` |
| Callback failure prevents Core admission | `callback failure prevents Core admission and leaves existing unchanged` |
| Callback side effects are outside Core atomicity | `callback side effects are outside Core atomicity` |
| The package-root adapter is exercised | `package-root adapter produces the exact C-1 claim through Core admission` |

`T18-DEC-15` remains OPEN. T18-02A uses Option B — one Assessment per `(child, relation)`, complete declared parent set, at least one parent absent — as a local implementation choice/disposition. This document does not present Option B as a normative interpretation of CORE-001.

## 2. Exact commands

```text
bun test tests/conformance/c.test.ts
bun test tests/unit/assessment-validation.test.ts tests/unit/orphan-assessment.test.ts tests/unit/lineage-graph.test.ts
bun test
bun run lint
bun run typecheck
bun run build
bun run format:check
```

## 3. Positive evidence

Test: `C-1 orphan ingestion records PARENT_UNRESOLVED in an Assessment`
File: `tests/conformance/c.test.ts`

Graph:

```text
iv-d ──MERGED_FROM──► iv-a   (present)
     └─MERGED_FROM──► iv-b   (absent)
```

The test imports `emitOrphanAssessment` from `src/index.ts`, supplies a caller-owned ID callback, and asserts:

- one registered Assessment;
- `unverified_claims` is exactly `['PARENT_UNRESOLVED']`;
- `parent_version_ids` is `['iv-a', 'iv-b']` — the complete declared parent set;
- `graph.unresolvedParents` is `[['iv-d', ['iv-b']]]`;
- the graph JSON is unchanged;
- the registered representation is frozen.

This is the C-1 positive path. The Assessment is constructed by the adapter, not by a test literal.

## 4. Mixed resolved/unresolved parent evidence

Tests:

- `emits one declaration-scoped assessment for mixed resolved and unresolved parents`
- `assessEdge returns the same assessment for resolved and unresolved edges`

Files:

- `tests/unit/orphan-assessment.test.ts`
- `tests/unit/assessment-validation.test.ts`

The same graph is used. The Assessment contains `['iv-a', 'iv-b']` and `PARENT_UNRESOLVED`. `assessEdge` returns the same Assessment for `iv-d → iv-a` (resolved) and `iv-d → iv-b` (unresolved). The test asserts that `iv-a` is present in the graph and that the claim remains declaration-scoped; it does not assert that `iv-d → iv-a` is unresolved.

This is the explicit distinction required by the approved plan: applicability to an edge does not transform a declaration-scoped claim into an edge-scoped claim. No `assessEdge` behavior was changed and no edge-scoped claim was introduced.

## 5. Negative evidence

Test: `C-1 resolved parent produces no PARENT_UNRESOLVED Assessment`
File: `tests/conformance/c.test.ts`

Graph: `iv-d MERGED_FROM iv-a, iv-b`, both parents present. The adapter returns `assessments: []` and `registered: []`; `graph.unresolvedParents` is empty.

Additional negative cases in `tests/unit/assessment-validation.test.ts`:

- strict subset of the declared parent set → rejected;
- undeclared parent → rejected;
- all parents resolved with a submitted candidate → rejected;
- `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` in `verified_claims` → rejected;
- `CYCLE_DETECTED` in a C-1 candidate → rejected;
- manually constructed graph → rejected;
- `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` through generic `registerAssessment` → rejected.

## 6. Generic vs contextual boundary

Generic `registerAssessment` validates structure and rejects `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` in either claim list. The C-1 contextual path validates the graph relationship and then admits. The tests in `tests/unit/assessment-validation.test.ts` assert both directions.

The `CONTEXT_REQUIRED_CLAIMS` set is admission metadata only. It is not read by `assessEdge`, `evaluateAssurance`, or `Policy`.

## 7. Atomicity and callback boundary

Tests:

- `admits all valid candidates as one frozen representation`
- `admits none when one candidate is invalid`
- `rejects duplicate IDs within the batch`
- `rejects duplicate IDs against existing assessments`
- `rejects unknown supersession references and cycles`
- `leaves the caller existing array and members unchanged on failure`
- `callback failure prevents Core admission and leaves existing unchanged`
- `callback side effects are outside Core atomicity`

Core admission returns either the complete frozen representation or no new representation. `existing` is deep-copied and never mutated. Callback side effects occur before Core admission and are not rolled back; caller-managed persistence occurs only after `ok: true`.

## 8. Graph provenance and Registry limitation

Test: `duplicate version ids with divergent lineage produce a builder-issued combined graph`
File: `tests/unit/lineage-graph.test.ts`

The test pins current structural behavior: duplicate version ids are deduplicated in `nodes`, while both declarations contribute edges. It asserts `isBuiltLineageGraph(graph)` is true. This documents the limitation that builder provenance does not imply descriptor validity; it does not approve contradictory Registry contents.

`buildLineageGraph` remains structural. Descriptor validation is a caller precondition. The C-1 contextual validator checks consistency with the supplied graph, not §5.2 declaration cardinality.

## 9. Package-root surface

Test: `package-root adapter produces the exact C-1 claim through Core admission`
File: `tests/unit/orphan-assessment.test.ts`

The test imports `emitOrphanAssessment` from `src/index.ts`. The adapter calls Core admission. The test also asserts that `registerOrphanAssessment`, `registerOrphanAssessments`, and `validateContinuityAssessment` are exported, and that `isBuiltLineageGraph` is not.

`emitOrphanAssessment` is an experimental reference adapter API. It is not a CORE-001 protocol API and carries no stability guarantee or compatibility commitment.

## 10. Recorded results

At the T18-02A implementation revision:

```text
bun test tests/conformance/c.test.ts
  2 pass, 1 todo, 0 fail

bun test
  548 pass, 3 todo, 0 fail, 3395 expect() calls, 26 files

bun run lint       pass
bun run typecheck  pass
bun run build      pass
bun run format:check pass
```

Task 17 artifacts and rollups are unchanged. C-1 remains NOT COVERED in the Task 17 audit; this document is Task 18 evidence, not a retrospective status rewrite. `T18-DEC-15` remains OPEN.

Index: docs/implementation.md
===================================================================
--- docs/implementation.md
+++ docs/implementation.md
@@ -721,9 +721,9 @@
 - Trusted assessors resolve as `requirement.trusted_assessors ?? policy.trustedAssessorDefault ?? []`. There is no trust-all default; an empty list means no assessment is trusted.
 - Only trusted assessments contribute verified claims. If `policy.conflictPredicate` is defined and fires for any pair, the result is `CONTESTED`; this check runs before the missing/disallowed computation. By default the predicate is `undefined`, so `CONTESTED` is unreachable.
 - `missing` is the sorted set of required claims absent from the union of verified claims; `disallowed` is the sorted set of verified claims listed in `disallowed_claims`. Either non-empty yields `UNSATISFIED` with `ERR_ASSURANCE_PREDICATE_UNSATISFIED` and the fixed `note`. No negative finding about a claim is established.
 - `unverified_claims` is not read by assurance evaluation at all: it neither supports nor refutes a required claim. Only `verified_claims` count.
-- `validateContinuityAssessment` is the generic runtime validator. It uses strict JSON/ownership validation, rejects unknown fields, requires the §6.2.1 fields, checks the relation enum, requires non-empty identifier strings, rejects duplicate/self parents, and requires a finite `assessed_at`. It returns an owned, deeply frozen copy. It does not interpret claim semantics.
+- `validateContinuityAssessment` is the generic runtime validator. It uses strict JSON/ownership validation, rejects unknown fields, requires the §6.2.1 fields, checks the relation enum, requires non-empty strings for identifiers, claims and evidence references, rejects duplicate/self parents, and requires a finite `assessed_at`. It returns an owned, deeply frozen copy. It does not interpret claim semantics.
 - `registerAssessment` is copy-on-write and validates its `unknown` successor before admission. It rejects `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` in either claim list with `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`; that claim is admission metadata, not claim semantics, and requires the C-1 contextual path.  - `validateContinuityAssessment` is the generic runtime validator. It uses strict JSON/ownership validation, rejects unknown fields, requires the §6.2.1 fields, checks the relation enum, requires non-empty strings for identifiers, claims and evidence references, rejects duplicate/self parents, and requires a finite `assessed_at`. It returns an owned, deeply frozen copy. It does not interpret claim semantics.
 - `registerAssessment` is copy-on-write and validates its `unknown` successor before admission. It rejects `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` in either claim list with `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`; that claim is admission metadata, not claim semantics, and requires the C-1 contextual path. A self-supersession or a supersession chain that would cycle returns `CYCLE_DETECTED`; a duplicate `assessment_id` or unknown `supersedes_assessment_id` returns `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`. Existing records are copied and frozen, never mutated.
 - `registerOrphanAssessments` is the C-1 atomic batch path. It requires a builder-issued graph, validates every candidate generically, then contextually, then admits all or none. The contextual rules are: the subject is in `graph.nodes`; the parent list is non-empty, unique and does not include the subject; the listed set equals the complete declared parent set for `(subject, declared_relation)`; at least one listed parent is absent from `graph.nodes`; every absent parent is recorded in `graph.unresolvedParents`; `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` is in `unverified_claims` and not in `verified_claims`; and the candidate does not claim `CYCLE_DETECTED`.
 - `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` is declaration-scoped, not edge-scoped. `assessEdge` may return the same Assessment for a resolved edge and an unresolved edge in the same declaration; that applicability does not make the resolved edge unresolved. `unverified_claims` remains unread by assurance evaluation.
-- Batch admission checks duplicate IDs within the batch and against `existing`, validates supersession references against the complete prospective state, and rejects cycles. On failure it returns no new representation; `existing` is unchanged. Callback side effects and caller-managed persistence are outside Core atomicity.

files.patch:
Index: docs/implementation.md
===================================================================
--- docs/implementation.md
+++ docs/implementation.md
@@ -721,9 +721,9 @@
 - Trusted assessors resolve as `requirement.trusted_assessors ?? policy.trustedAssessorDefault ?? []`. There is no trust-all default; an empty list means no assessment is trusted.
 - Only trusted assessments contribute verified claims. If `policy.conflictPredicate` is defined and fires for any pair, the result is `CONTESTED`; this check runs before the missing/disallowed computation. By default the predicate is `undefined`, so `CONTESTED` is unreachable.
 - `missing` is the sorted set of required claims absent from the union of verified claims; `disallowed` is the sorted set of verified claims listed in `disallowed_claims`. Either non-empty yields `UNSATISFIED` with `ERR_ASSURANCE_PREDICATE_UNSATISFIED` and the fixed `note`. No negative finding about a claim is established.
 - `unverified_claims` is not read by assurance evaluation at all: it neither supports nor refutes a required claim. Only `verified_claims` count.
-- `validateContinuityAssessment` is the generic runtime validator. It uses strict JSON/ownership validation, rejects unknown fields, requires the §6.2.1 fields, checks the relation enum, requires non-empty strings for identifiers, claims and evidence references, rejects duplicate/self parents, and requires a finite `assessed_at`. It returns an owned, deeply frozen copy. It does not interpret claim semantics.
+- `validateContinuityAssessment` is the generic runtime validator. It uses strict JSON/ownership validation, rejects unknown fields, requires the §6.2.1 fields, checks the relation enum, requires non-empty identifier strings and non-empty parent IDs, requires claim and evidence arrays of strings, rejects duplicate/self parents, and requires a finite `assessed_at`. It returns an owned, deeply frozen copy. It does not interpret claim semantics.
 - `registerAssessment` is copy-on-write and validates its `unknown` successor before admission. It rejects `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` in either claim list with `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`; that claim is admission metadata, not claim semantics, and requires the C-1 contextual path. A self-supersession or a supersession chain that would cycle returns `CYCLE_DETECTED`; a duplicate `assessment_id` or unknown `supersedes_assessment_id` returns `E_UNKNOWN_BOUNDARY_REJECTED`. Existing records are copied and frozen, never mutated.
 - `registerOrphanAssessments` is the C-1 atomic batch path. It requires a builder-issued graph, validates every candidate generically, then contextually, then admits all or none. The contextual rules are: the subject is in `graph.nodes`; the parent list is non-empty, unique and does not include the subject; the listed set equals the complete declared parent set for `(subject, declared_relation)`; at least one listed parent is absent from `graph.nodes`; every absent parent is recorded in `graph.unresolvedParents`; `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` is in `unverified_claims` and not in `verified_claims`; and the candidate does not claim `CYCLE_DETECTED`.
 - `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` is declaration-scoped, not edge-scoped. `assessEdge` may return the same Assessment for a resolved edge and an unresolved edge in the same declaration; that applicability does not make the resolved edge unresolved. `unverified_claims` remains unread by assurance evaluation.
 - Batch admission checks duplicate IDs within the batch, against `existing`, and within `existing` itself; validates supersession references against the complete prospective state; and rejects cycles. On failure it returns no new representation; `existing` is unchanged. Callback side effects and caller-managed persistence are outside Core atomicity.

## 1. Decision process

### Validation enforcement

Mandatory Core validation at the registration boundary is approved. - Persistent storage, publication and retention ownership.
- C-2 `CYCLE_DETECTED` admission policy (T18-02B; not part of T18-02A).
- Parent-coverage semantics (`T18-DEC-15`).
- C-2.a3 grant suppression and other cross-specification decisions, including CORE-003.

<skill_content name="ship">
# Skill: ship

# ship

Цель — PR зелёный, все ревью отработаны, merge сделан **после «Мерджим» пользователя**,
за собой ничего не осталось. Прод в цель **не входит**: он выкатывается только по явному
слову пользователя в этой сессии.

## 0. Где ты

- Работа идёт в git worktree, не в основном checkout; ветка `<type>/<issue#>-<slug>`.
- Алиас репозитория и команды — только из `run.sh <alias> list`, не из памяти.
  У `owner-api` проверки запускаются из `owner-api/ownima-backend/`.

## 1. До пуша

1. Точечные проверки, не полный прогон (машина: 4 ядра, 7 ГБ):
   `bash .claude/skills/repo-checks/scripts/run.sh <alias> fast` плюс `lint`.
   Команды скрипт берёт из своей матрицы, поэтому запускай его из корня workspace.
   Если падает на импорте — сначала `run.sh <alias> doctor`, это может быть несинхронный venv.
2. Самопроверка дифа по чек-листу «A change is done when every surface it touches has it»
   из корневого `AGENTS.md`. Пройди по каждому пункту и назови, что проверил:
   все виды сущности в UI, публичные и кэшируемые ответы, поиск против настоящего
   OpenSearch, аккаунты, которые отсекают фильтры прод-скриптов.
3. Если менялся ответ API — перегенерированы ли типы во фронтах, которые его читают.

## 2. PR

- `gh pr create` с заголовком в Conventional Commits, тело на английском, `Closes #N`,
  межрепозиторные ссылки полными URL. Тело заканчивается строкой атрибуции из системных
  инструкций.
- Если PR уже есть — работай с ним, не открывай второй.

## 3. CI

- Ждать: `gh pr checks <N> --watch --fail-fast` в фоне (`run_in_background`), не опрашивать
  в цикле.
- Упало — читать лог упавшего job: `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`. Классифицировать:
  - превышен только бюджет времени / явный флейк → `gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`, **один раз**;
  - устаревший сгенерированный артефакт (OpenAPI-снимок, lockfile) → перегенерировать, запушить;
  - ветка отстала от `main` → `gh pr update-branch <N>` (закрыть и переоткрыть PR merge-ref
    не обновляет);
  - падение не связано с PR (скан уязвимостей на `main`) → записать и сказать пользователю;
  - настоящая регрессия → чинить с тестом, как обычную ошибку.
- Job висит в `queued` и не падает — значит, нет живого runner с его меткой: проверки идут
  на `ci-ownima` (`ci`), деплой — на `worker-ownima` (`worker`). Это runner, а не код;
  почему какой job где — в комментариях `ansible/inventories/infra/host_vars/`.

## 4. Ревью — все, а не только человеческие

Комментарии лежат в трёх местах, читать все три:

```
gh api repos/Ownima/<repo>/pulls/<N>/comments --paginate   # построчные
gh api repos/Ownima/<repo>/pulls/<N>/reviews  --paginate   # ревью целиком
gh api repos/Ownima/<repo>/issues/<N>/comments --paginate  # общий тред (Sonar, Semgrep)
```

- Каждый комментарий Gemini, Sonar, Semgrep и людей: исправить или ответить, почему нет.
- Отвечать **после** пуша исправления и ссылаться на реальный короткий хеш коммита.
- После пуша — снова шаг 3.

## 5. Merge

- Только когда все обязательные проверки зелёные и ревью отработаны.
- **Перед merge — остановиться и спросить.** Показать: PR, статус CI, какие ревью
  отработаны и какими коммитами. Мержить только после явного «Мерджим» (или «мержи»)
  на **этот** PR в этой сессии. Фраза «merge on green» в задаче и согласие на прошлый PR
  не в счёт: правило пользователя — решение на каждый merge отдельно.
- `gh pr merge <N> --squash --delete-branch` (история `main` у owner-api — только squash;
  в остальных squash тоже по умолчанию).

## 6. Уборка

```
git worktree remove <path>        # не --force: грязный worktree — повод спросить
git branch -D <branch>
git fetch --prune
```

## 7. Релиз — здесь репозитории различаются

| Репозиторий | Merge фичи | Merge релизного PR release-please |
|---|---|---|
| `owner-api` | ничего не деплоит | тег `vX.Y.Z` → **staging**. Прод — отдельный ручной шаг (см. `owner-api/AGENTS.md`), только по слову пользователя |
| `owner-web` | **staging** (push в `main`) | release published → **прод** (`release.yml` → `deploy-prod.yml`) |
| `booking-web`, `rider-app` | — | release published → **прод** (`release.yml`) |
| `owner-admin` | **прод** (Vercel деплоит каждый push в `main`) | release-please нет |
| остальные | release-please нет | — |

- Релизный PR фронта **не мержить без явного «да»** — это выкатка на прод.
- В `owner-admin` любой merge — прод. Перед вопросом «Мерджим» открыть Vercel preview
  из комментария `vercel[bot]` на затронутых страницах и сказать об этом пользователю.
- Коммиты release-please с версиями не переписывать (`reset`, `rebase`, `amend`).
- Релизный PR owner-api — тоже только после «Мерджим» (он выкатывает staging).

## 8. Smoke на staging

После деплоя на staging дождаться окончания workflow, затем:

```
bash .claude/skills/ship/scripts/smoke.sh <path> [<path> ...]   # пути под /api/v1
```

Перечислить **каждый** эндпоинт, который трогало изменение. Скрипт ждёт 2xx и непустое
тело (`[]`, `{}`, пустой `data`/`items` — провал), пустой ответ перепроверяет один раз.
Он только читает и только на staging. Логинится как showcase-owner, если есть
`~/.config/ownima/smoke.env` (`SMOKE_EMAIL`, `SMOKE_PASSWORD`, права 600); без него
проверяет без авторизации, и закрытые эндпоинты дадут 401 — так и сказать, не выдавать
за успех. Экраны фронта смотреть в браузере. Без зелёного smoke «на стейдже» не говорить.

**Постоянный набор и трассы — одной командой** (на «прогони смок и трейс на stage», алиас `smk`):

```
bash .claude/skills/ship/scripts/stage-check.sh [<flow> ...] [-- <доп. путь> ...]
```

1. `smoke.sh --default`: пути из `scripts/smoke-default.txt` (me, гараж, брони, шаблоны,
   extras, баланс, транзакции, каталог) плюс те, что даны после `--`. Набор правится в
   файле; путь, законно пустой у showcase, туда не кладут.
2. Трассы (`ownima-backend/app/scripts/trace`) в контейнере stage: `booking`, `pricing`,
   `rider_booking`, или только названные. Они **пишут** на stage через настоящий API и
   убирают за собой; у каждого flow свой Redis-лок, так что запуск поверх трассы деплоя
   скажет «занято», а не «прошло».

Итог одной строкой, выход 0 / 1 (провал) / 2 (не запустилось). Изменение, которого нет в
наборе, проверяется своими путями: `stage-check.sh -- price_template/<id>/season`.

## 9. Если что-то заблокировано

Merge, удаление ветки, прод-команду, на которую auto-mode ответил отказом, не обходить
другим способом. Собрать все такие команды и в конце выдать одним блоком для `! …`.

## 10. Отчёт

Коротко: PR (URL), что было в CI и что сделано, какие ревью отработаны и какими коммитами,
где сейчас изменение (main / staging / ждёт прод), что ждёт решения пользователя.

Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.
Note: file list is sampled.

</skill_content>

# Skill: receiving-code-review

# Code Review Reception

## Overview

Code review requires technical evaluation, not emotional performance.

**Core principle:** Verify before implementing. Ask before assuming. Technical correctness over social comfort.

## The Response Pattern

```
WHEN receiving code review feedback:

1. READ: Complete feedback without reacting
2. UNDERSTAND: Restate requirement in own words (or ask)
3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality
4. EVALUATE: Technically sound for THIS codebase?
5. RESPOND: Technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback
6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each
```

## Forbidden Responses

**NEVER:**
- "You're absolutely right!" (explicit instruction-file violation)
- "Great point!" / "Excellent feedback!" (performative)
- "Let me implement that now" (before verification)

**INSTEAD:**
- Restate the technical requirement
- Ask clarifying questions
- Push back with technical reasoning if wrong
- Just start working (actions > words)

## Handling Unclear Feedback

```
IF any item is unclear:
  STOP - do not implement anything yet
  ASK for clarification on unclear items

WHY: Items may be related. Partial understanding = wrong implementation.
```

**Example:**
```
your human partner: "Fix 1-6"
You understand 1,2,3,6. Unclear on 4,5.

❌ WRONG: Implement 1,2,3,6 now, ask about 4,5 later
✅ RIGHT: "I understand items 1,2,3,6. Need clarification on 4 and 5 before proceeding."
```

## Source-Specific Handling

### From your human partner
- **Trusted** - implement after understanding
- **Still ask** if scope unclear
- **No performative agreement**
- **Skip to action** or technical acknowledgment

### From External Reviewers
```
BEFORE implementing:
  1. Check: Technically correct for THIS codebase?
  2. Check: Breaks existing functionality?
  3. Check: Reason for current implementation?
  4. Check: Works on all platforms/versions?
  5. Check: Does reviewer understand full context?

IF suggestion seems wrong:
  Push back with technical reasoning

IF can't easily verify:
  Say so: "I can't verify this without [X]. Should I [investigate/ask/proceed]?"

IF conflicts with your human partner's prior decisions:
  Stop and discuss with your human partner first
```

**your human partner's rule:** "External feedback - be skeptical, but check carefully"

## YAGNI Check for "Professional" Features

```
IF reviewer suggests "implementing properly":
  grep codebase for actual usage

  IF unused: "This endpoint isn't called. Remove it (YAGNI)?"
  IF used: Then implement properly
```

**your human partner's rule:** "You and reviewer both report to me. If we don't need this feature, don't add it."

## Implementation Order

```
FOR multi-item feedback:
  1. Clarify anything unclear FIRST
  2. Then implement in this order:
     - Blocking issues (breaks, security)
     - Simple fixes (typos, imports)
     - Complex fixes (refactoring, logic)
  3. Test each fix individually
  4. Verify no regressions
```

## When To Push Back

Push back when:
- Suggestion breaks existing functionality
- Reviewer lacks full context
- Violates YAGNI (unused feature)
- Technically incorrect for this stack
- Legacy/compatibility reasons exist
- Conflicts with your human partner's architectural decisions

**How to push back:**
- Use technical reasoning, not defensiveness
- Ask specific questions

# Code Review Reception

## Overview

Code review requires technical evaluation, not emotional performance.

## The Response Pattern

```

3. VERIFY: Check against codebase reality
4. EVALUATE: Technically sound for THIS codebase?
5. RESPOND: Technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback
6. IMPLEMENT: One item at a time, test each
```

- "Great point!" / "Excellent feedback!" (performative)

- Push back with technical reasoning if wrong

 **Semantics**
 
 - The adapter groups `graph.edges` by `(child, relation)` for the requested child, includes the complete declared parent set for each group, and emits only groups with at least one parent absent from `graph.nodes`.
 - `assessmentIdFor` is called once per emitted group, in sorted relation order and sorted parent order. The adapter validates the returned ID as a non-empty string. It does not generate IDs.
-- The adapter calls `registerOrphanAssessments` once for the complete batch. It stops before Core admission if the graph is not builder-issued, the child is absent, the callback throws, or an ID is invalid. A callback exception is reported as a mechanism failure that includes the original error message when available.
+- The adapter calls `registerOrphanAssessments` once for the complete batch, including an empty batch. It stops before Core admission if the graph is not builder-issued, the child is absent, the callback throws, or an ID is invalid. A callback exception is reported as a mechanism failure that includes the original error message when available.
+- Even when no orphan candidate is emitted, the returned `registered` value is a Core-owned frozen copy, not the caller's mutable `existing` array. The emission object is frozen.
 - The returned `assessments` are the admitted tail of the frozen registered representation; `registered` is the complete frozen representation.
 - `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` is declaration-scoped. Applicability of the Assessment to a resolved edge does not make that edge unresolved.
 - Callback side effects are outside Core atomicity and are not rolled back. Caller persistence occurs only after successful admission.

## Plan Mode — Evidence-Based Investigation Only

You are working in the `zaebee/federation-agents` repository.

Task: T18-09A from the approved Task 18 remediation roadmap.

**Mode: Plan Mode only.**

Do not modify files. Do not implement code. Do not create branches, commits, or pull requests. Do not edit `docs/CORE-001.md` or any Task 17 artifact.

Your goal is to prepare two evidence-based project-owner decision packages for unresolved assurance semantics:

- T18-DEC-06 — contradictory trusted assessments (AMBIG-A-4b).
- T18-DEC-07 — closure depth (AMBIG-A-5).

These are separate normative questions. Do not assume that choosing one determines the other.

---

Before reasoning:

1. Inspect the current `main` HEAD and working tree state.
2. Confirm that T18-02A has been merged.
3. Read the current versions of:
   - `docs/CORE-001.md`
   - `docs/implementation.md`
   - `docs/audits/2026-10-31-core-001-task-18/README.md`
   - `disposition-matrix.md`
   - `remediation-roadmap.md`

   - `src/core/assessment.ts`
   - `src/core/traversal.ts`

   - relevant unit, property, and conformance tests.

Use the current repository as the source of truth. Do not rely on remembered line numbers or prior plans.

Source hierarchy:

1. Approved normative specification (`docs/CORE-001.md`).

# 1. T18-DEC-06 — Contradictory trusted assessments

Related ambiguity: `AMBIG-A-4b`.

Related requirements from Task 17: N-078, N-107, N-172.

## 1.1 Establish exact normative evidence

Locate and quote the smallest relevant excerpts from CORE-001, including:

- definitions of `ContinuityAssessment`;
- `verified_claims` and `unverified_claims`;
- trusted assessor / applicable assessment semantics;
- assurance evaluation rules;
- treatment of multiple applicable Assessments;
- all relevant conformance examples and constraints.

Identify exactly what the specification says and, equally importantly, what it does not define.

Do not infer that "trusted" automatically means "non-contradictory".

## 1.2 Establish current implementation behavior

Trace the full execution path:

- Assessment selection and applicability (`assessEdge` or equivalent);
- trust filtering;
- `evaluateAssurance`;
- verified-claim aggregation;
- policy narrowing;
- treatment of missing, contradictory, or contested claims;
- interaction with traversal and merge closure.

Use concrete code references and tests.

Determine whether current code:

- accepts two trusted Assessments with contradictory claims;
- rejects them;
- treats them as independent evidence;
- silently chooses one;
- depends on ordering;
- can produce different results after reordering equivalent inputs.

Do not assume a behavior without a test or a direct code trace.

## 1.3 Develop independent semantic alternatives

At minimum, analyze:

**Option A — Conflict means CONTESTED**

If two applicable trusted Assessments make mutually incompatible assertions about the same semantic subject, the relevant assurance outcome becomes `CONTESTED`.

**Option B — Claims are independent observations**

Assessments remain independent records. A contradiction is not automatically a conflict unless a specific policy or claim relation establishes incompatibility.

**Option C — Explicit conflict predicate**

Define a conflict predicate based on a narrowly specified set of conditions, such as:
- same subject;
- same declared relation;
- same assessment scope;
- mutually exclusive claims;
- both Assessments trusted and applicable.

Do not assume these conditions are correct. Evaluate whether CORE-001 supports them.

You may propose another option if the specification or code requires it.

For each option explain:

- normative support;
- what counts as a contradiction;
- whether claims are compared within one Assessment or across Assessments;
- whether `verified` versus `unverified` claims can conflict;
- whether two different assessors matter;
- how supersession affects conflict;
- whether timestamps or ordering matter;
- whether conflict is local to an edge, declaration, subject, or traversal;
- effect on `evaluateAssurance`;
- effect on `ApplicableAssessments`;
- effect on existing consumers;
- false-positive and false-negative risks;
- adversarial examples.

Do not invent a universal logical contradiction engine if the protocol only defines a small set of claim semantics.

## 1.4 Required adversarial cases

At minimum analyze:

1. Two trusted Assessments, same subject and relation, one verifies claim X and another verifies an incompatible claim Y.
2. One Assessment verifies X, another marks X unverified.
3. One Assessment verifies X, another contains X in neither list.
4. Two Assessments from the same assessor contradict each other.
5. Two Assessments from different assessors contradict each other.
6. A newer Assessment supersedes an older contradictory Assessment.
7. A newer Assessment does not supersede an older contradictory Assessment.
8. Two Assessments differ only in ordering of claim arrays.
9. Two Assessments apply to different parent edges of the same merge declaration.
10. One Assessment is trusted, the other is not.
11. One Assessment is applicable, the other is not.
12. The same claim appears in both `verified_claims` and `unverified_claims` within one malformed or boundary-supplied Assessment.

For every case state the expected result under each viable option. If the specification does not determine the result, mark it OPEN.

## 1.5 Decision package output

Prepare a proposed decision record for T18-DEC-06 with:

- decision question;
- exact normative evidence;
- implementation evidence;
- options;
- trade-offs;
- adversarial cases;
- recommended option and rationale;
- consequences for future tests and implementation;
- whether a CORE-001 amendment is required.

Recommendation is not approval. Keep the decision OPEN.

---

# 2. T18-DEC-07 — Closure depth

Related ambiguity: `AMBIG-A-5`.

Related requirement: N-112.

## 2.1 Establish exact normative evidence

Locate relevant CORE-001 passages for:

- path validation;
- merge closure;
- parent-edge assessments;
- immediate parent requirements;
- recursive or transitive closure, if any;
- termination and cycle behavior;
- assurance evaluation order.

Determine whether "closure" is defined normatively or only used descriptively.

Distinguish:
- validating the selected path;
- validating direct parents of a merge node;
- recursively validating parents of those parents;
- traversing the entire ancestry graph.

Do not treat these as equivalent.

## 2.2 Establish current implementation behavior

Trace `validateMergeClosure` and all callers.

Confirm:

- which nodes trigger closure;
- which parent edges are checked;
- whether the exact path edge is excluded;
- whether mixed relation edges are included;
- whether recursion occurs;
- whether cycles can cause repeated work or non-termination;
- what evidence is retained in successful and failed results;
- whether scope policy changes discovery, closure, or both.

Inspect tests, especially:
- direct parent missing assessment;
- deeper ancestor missing assessment;
- mixed relation edges;
- merge node reached through a non-merge relation;
- multiple merge nodes along one path;
- cycles and graph invariance.

Use actual test names and code references.

## 2.3 Analyze independent closure alternatives

At minimum:

**Option A — Immediate closure**

For each merge node on the selected path, validate all its direct parent edges, excluding only the exact path edge. Do not recursively validate the ancestry of those parents unless they are independently encountered as merge nodes on the selected path.

**Option B — Recursive closure**

Continue validation recursively through parent branches until a defined stopping condition is reached.

**Option C — Bounded/transitive closure**

Define an explicit bounded or policy-controlled closure depth.

You may propose another option if justified by the normative text.

For each option analyze:

- exact meaning;
- normative support;
- termination guarantees;
- cycle behavior;
- complexity and resource bounds;
- interaction with scope;
- behavior on DAGs and cyclic graphs;
- evidence retention;
- compatibility with current API;
- false-positive and false-negative risks;
- possible denial-of-service implications;
- whether depth belongs to CORE-001 or a local policy.

Do not introduce a recursion-depth parameter merely because it is convenient to implement.

## 2.4 Required adversarial graph cases

At minimum:

1. Simple merge with all direct parent assessments present.
2. Direct parent assessment missing.
3. Direct parent itself has a missing parent.
4. Deep unresolved ancestor several levels below a merge.
5. Nested merge where all immediate assessments pass but a deeper merge fails.
6. Multiple merge nodes along the selected path.
7. Same graph reached through different valid paths.
8. Mixed relation parent edges.
9. Cyclic graph.
10. A merge node reached through a non-merge relation.
11. Scope excludes a parent from discovery but closure semantics may still require it.
12. Large/deep graph to evaluate resource bounds.

For each case state the expected result under each viable option. Mark normative ambiguity explicitly.

## 2.5 Decision package output

Prepare a proposed decision record for T18-DEC-07 with:

- decision question;
- exact normative evidence;
- implementation evidence;
- options;
- trade-offs;
- adversarial cases;
- recommended option and rationale;
- consequences for tests and implementation;
- whether a CORE-001 amendment is required.

Recommendation is not approval. Keep the decision OPEN.

---

# 3. Interaction between DEC-06 and DEC-07

Analyze the interaction, but do not collapse the decisions.

In particular:

- Does recursive closure multiply the effect of contradictory Assessments?
- Can a local CONTESTED result propagate through recursive closure?
- Does immediate closure limit the scope of conflict?
- Can a conflict on a non-path parent edge affect a path result?
- Can scope policy suppress discovery but still leave a closure obligation?
- Does either decision require changing `ApplicableAssessments` or only the evaluation algorithm?

Present a two-dimensional matrix:

| | Immediate closure | Recursive closure | Bounded closure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conflict → CONTESTED | ... | ... | ... |
| Independent claims | ... | ... | ... |
| Explicit conflict predicate | ... | ... | ... |

Mark unresolved combinations rather than guessing.

---

# 4. Cross-check against existing decisions and invariants

Verify that proposed options do not silently violate:

- Evidence ≠ Finding ≠ Ruling ≠ Execution Authorization.
- External findings do not automatically bind receiving domains.
- Identity lineage does not imply authority inheritance.
- ApplicableAssessments nominal brand and runtime validation.
- B-5 untrusted-assessment exclusion.
- Policy narrowing cannot reintroduce untrusted Assessments.
- Missing verified claim remains an actual UNSATISFIED reason.
- A-4b and A-5 remain separate questions.
- No automatic revocation.
- No grant-producing API in CORE-001.
- No implementation fiat for BLOCKED normative questions.

Also verify consistency with T18-02A:
- Do not change its implementation.
- Do not retrospectively alter Task 17.
- Keep T18-DEC-15 OPEN.
- Do not treat local Option B for `parent_version_ids` as a normative resolution.

---

# 5. Proposed deliverables

Do not create them yet. Specify exact proposed files and sections for a future docs-only decision package.

Prefer one package directory:

`docs/audits/2026-10-31-core-001-task-18/T18-09A/`

Proposed files:

1. `README.md` — scope, findings, decision status.
2. `dec-06-contradictory-assessments.md`
3. `dec-07-closure-depth.md`
4. `interaction-matrix.md`
5. `evidence-index.md` — source references and test inventory.

If the current roadmap or repository convention requires a different location, explain why.

Each decision file must distinguish:
- normative evidence;
- implementation evidence;
- interpretation;
- recommendation;
- project-owner decision;
- required spec amendment;
- downstream implementation tasks.

Do not edit existing Task 18 files in this phase.

---

# 6. Final response format

Return:

1. Repository state and revision.
2. Normative evidence for DEC-06.
3. Implementation behavior for DEC-06.
4. Options and adversarial matrix for DEC-06.
5. Normative evidence for DEC-07.
6. Implementation behavior for DEC-07.
7. Options and adversarial matrix for DEC-07.
8. Interaction matrix.
9. Invariant/cross-decision check.
10. Recommended project-owner decisions.
11. Proposed deliverables and dependencies.
12. Explicit OPEN/BLOCKED items.
13. Exact next step after project-owner review.

Use precise file paths, line references, function names, and test names. Cite the source of every factual claim.

Do not write generic summaries in place of code tracing.

---

# 7. Final constraints

- No files modified.
- No tests run unless needed for investigation; if run, report exact commands and results.
- No implementation plan that assumes decisions are approved.
- No CORE-001 edits.
- No Task 17 edits.
- No commits, branches, PRs, or GitHub reviews.
- Do not change decision statuses.
- Do not mark either decision APPROVED.
- Keep T18-DEC-06 and T18-DEC-07 OPEN.
- If evidence is insufficient, say so explicitly.
- Do not resolve ambiguity through implementation convenience.

Final gate: **EVIDENCE-BASED DECISION PACKAGE READY FOR PROJECT-OWNER REVIEW**, or explain exactly what prevents that status.

## 1.2 Establish current implementation behavior

- Assessment selection and applicability (`assessEdge` or equivalent);
- trust filtering;
- `evaluateAssurance`;
- verified-claim aggregation;
- policy narrowing;
- treatment of missing, contradictory, or contested claims;
- interaction with traversal and merge closure.

Use concrete code references and tests.

Determine whether current code:

- accepts two trusted Assessments with contradictory claims;
- rejects them;
- treats them as independent evidence;
- silently chooses one;
- depends on ordering;
- can produce different results after reordering equivalent inputs.

Do not assume a behavior without a test or a direct code trace.

## 1.3 Develop independent semantic alternatives

At minimum, analyze:

**Option A — Conflict means CONTESTED**

If two applicable trusted Assessments make mutually incompatible assertions about the same semantic subject, the relevant assurance outcome becomes `CONTESTED`.

**Option B — Claims are independent observations**

Assessments remain independent records. A contradiction is not automatically a conflict unless a specific policy or claim relation establishes incompatibility.

**Option C — Explicit conflict predicate**

Define a conflict predicate based on a narrowly specified set of conditions, such as:
- same subject;
- same declared relation;
- same assessment scope;
- mutually exclusive claims;
- both Assessments trusted and applicable.

Do not assume these conditions are correct. Evaluate whether CORE-001 supports them.

You may propose another option if the specification or code requires it.

For each option explain:

- normative support;
- what counts as a contradiction;
- whether claims are compared within one Assessment or across Assessments;
- whether `verified` versus `unverified` claims can conflict;
- whether two different assessors matter;
- how supersession affects conflict;
- whether timestamps or ordering matter;
- whether conflict is local to an edge, declaration, subject, or traversal;
- effect on `evaluateAssurance`;
- effect on `ApplicableAssessments`;
- effect on existing consumers;
- false-positive and false-negative risks;
- adversarial examples.

Do not invent a universal logical contradiction engine if the protocol only defines a small set of claim semantics.

1. Two trusted Assessments, same subject and relation, one verifies claim X and another verifies an incompatible claim Y.
2. One Assessment verifies X, another marks X unverified.
3. One Assessment verifies X, another contains X in neither list.
4. Two Assessments from the same assessor contradict each other.
5. Two Assessments from different assessors contradict each other.
6. A newer Assessment supersedes an older contradictory Assessment.
7. A newer Assessment does not supersede an older contradictory Assessment.
8. Two Assessments differ only in ordering of claim arrays.
9. Two Assessments apply to different parent edges of the same merge declaration.
10. One Assessment is trusted, the other is not.
11. One Assessment is applicable, the other is not.
12. The same claim appears in both `verified_claims` and `unverified_claims` within one malformed or boundary-supplied Assessment.

For every case state the expected result under each viable option. If the specification does not determine the result, mark it OPEN.

## 1.5 Decision package output

- decision question;
- exact normative evidence;
- implementation evidence;
- options;
- trade-offs;
- adversarial cases;
- recommended option and rationale;
- consequences for future tests and implementation;
- whether a CORE-001 amendment is required.

Recommendation is not approval. Keep the decision OPEN.

- path validation;
- merge closure;
- parent-edge assessments;
- immediate parent requirements;
- recursive or transitive closure, if any;
- termination and cycle behavior;

Determine whether "closure" is defined normatively or only used descriptively.

- validating the selected path;
- validating direct parents of a merge node;
- recursively validating parents of those parents;
- traversing the entire ancestry graph.

Do not treat these as equivalent.

Trace `validateMergeClosure` and all callers.

Confirm:

- which nodes trigger closure;
- which parent edges are checked;
- whether the exact path edge is excluded;
- whether mixed relation edges are included;
- whether recursion occurs;
- whether cycles can cause repeated work or non-termination;
- what evidence is retained in successful and failed results;

Inspect tests, especially:

- mixed relation edges;

Use actual test names and code references.

**Option A — Immediate closure**

# Decision Register — Task 18

**Audit base:** `2a83c65`.
**Status of decisions:** 2 APPROVED (`T18-DEC-01`, `T18-DEC-02`); 13 OPEN.

This register records the normative and boundary questions. Approved resolutions are recorded in §3; all other decisions remain OPEN.

## 1. Decision process

1. A decision is proposed with the question, normative anchor, owner and required evidence.
2. The owner records a proposed resolution and its consequences.
3. If the resolution requires a CORE-001 amendment, it goes through separately approved `T18-SPEC-01`.
4. Dependent implementation tasks remain conditional until the decision is approved.
5. Approval is recorded in this register when the project owner explicitly approves. A proposal is not an approval.

Status values: `APPROVED` (explicit project-owner approval recorded here) or `OPEN` (no approved resolution).

## 3. Approved decisions

### T18-DEC-01 — `REQ-LOCAL`

CORE-001 requires a local Assessment recording:

- `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` for an unresolved parent;
- `CYCLE_DETECTED` for a detected cycle.

This is an obligation to record the condition. It does not, by itself, assign construction or publication responsibility to Core. Approval is not conformance evidence and does not change Task 17 statuses.

### T18-DEC-02 — `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE` (Core-owned admission/representation)

- Adapter owns Assessment construction using domain-specific identity, provenance and time context.
- Core owns normative semantic validation.
- Core validation MUST be enforced on every supported registration path.
- A standalone validator that callers can bypass is insufficient.
- An old public registration API MUST NOT remain a validation bypass.
- Publication and retention remain separate responsibilities and must be explicitly assigned by the relevant boundary.
- Downstream consumption does not automatically accept the Assessment as truth or grant authority.

**Scope of approval:** DEC-02 assigns adapter **construction**, Core **semantic validation**, and Core-owned **admission** with an **immutable registered representation**. The adapter constructs candidates and initiates admission through the Core API; it must not mutate admitted state. Persistent storage is **caller-managed**. Publication and retention remain **OPEN**. This paragraph is the canonical scope statement; other documents should reference it rather than paraphrase.

### Validation enforcement

Mandatory Core validation at the registration boundary is approved. The implementation design may choose between validation inside `registerAssessment` or a guarded validated-registration API, provided the old public API cannot bypass validation. No further implementation detail is approved by this decision.

### T18-DEC-15 — parent coverage semantics (OPEN)

CORE-001 does not state whether `ContinuityAssessment.parent_version_ids` must equal the full declared parent set for `(subject_version_id, declared_relation)` or may be the subset covered by the Assessment.

T18-02A uses **Option B** — one Assessment per `(child, relation)`, with the complete declared parent set and at least one parent absent from the local graph — as a **local implementation choice/disposition**. This is not a resolution of the normative question. The question remains OPEN and requires a separate `T18-SPEC-01` clarification before either model is described as normative.

The `Resolution` column is the register's generic field name. For `T18-DEC-15` it records a non-normative local disposition, not a normative resolution.

### Still open

- C-2 Assessment subject model: SCC, node, or edge. Edge-level is a proposal only.
- Exact Assessment data shape and provenance contract.
- Persistent storage, publication and retention ownership.
- C-2 `CYCLE_DETECTED` admission policy (T18-02B; not part of T18-02A).
- Parent-coverage semantics (`T18-DEC-15`).
- C-2.a3 grant suppression and other cross-specification decisions, including CORE-003.

### Path correction

`VAL-CORE-CONSTRUCTION` is only compatible with `OWN-CORE`. It is not a valid option under `OWN-ADAPTER`. The selected path is `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE`.

## 4. Ambiguity mapping

Task 17 ambiguity identifiers are preserved exactly. They are not renamed and not re-scoped.

| Ambiguity | Status | Related Task 18 decision | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AMBIG-A-1 | OPEN (mechanism) | — | Selector grammar remains a versioned mechanism |
| AMBIG-A-2 | OPEN | — | “EXACT” binding mode remains open; B-1 PASS is based on observable result |
| AMBIG-A-3 / AMBIG-A-6 | OPEN | — | Mixed relation types |
| AMBIG-A-4a | Resolved by literal text | — | Unverified claims: no positive support, no negative finding |
| AMBIG-A-4b | BLOCKED | T18-DEC-06 | Contradiction predicate |
| AMBIG-A-5 | BLOCKED | T18-DEC-07 | Closure depth |
| AMBIG-A-7 | OPEN | T18-DEC-08 | `CONTENT_HASH` format |
| AMBIG-A-8 | OPEN | — | Aggregation beyond B-4 |
| AMBIG-A-9 | BLOCKED (external) | T18-DEC-09 | Trusted-time mechanism |
| AMBIG-A-10 | Resolved by implementation semantics | — | Scope vs closure |
| AMBIG-A-11 | BLOCKED | — | Origin closure; no Task 18 decision is created because it is not a non-PASS requirement row |
| AMBIG-A-12 | Out of scope | — | Crypto verification |

`T18-DEC-04` is a Task 18 decision about the §4.4.1 precondition. It is deliberately **not** mapped to AMBIG-A-9, which concerns the mechanism. No new Task 17 ambiguity ID is created.

## 5. Rules

- A decision is not approved because an implementation already behaves a certain way.
- A decision is not approved because a test passes.
- A decision that changes normative text requires `T18-SPEC-01` and a re-audit.
- A decision that assigns responsibility to another specification requires that specification’s owner and acceptance criteria.
- A decision that assigns responsibility to an external system requires an explicit interface and evidence expectations.

**Audit base:** `2a83c65`.
**Status of decisions:** 2 APPROVED (`T18-DEC-01`, `T18-DEC-02`); 13 OPEN.

This register records the normative and boundary questions. Approved resolutions are recorded in §3; all other decisions remain OPEN.

## 1. Decision process

1. A decision is proposed with the question, normative anchor, owner and required evidence.

## 3. Approved decisions

### T18-DEC-01 — `REQ-LOCAL`

CORE-001 requires a local Assessment recording:

- `PARENT_UNRESOLVED` for an unresolved parent;
- `CYCLE_DETECTED` for a detected cycle.

This is an obligation to record the condition. It does not, by itself, assign construction or publication responsibility to Core. Approval is not conformance evidence and does not change Task 17 statuses.

### T18-DEC-02 — `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE` (Core-owned admission/representation)

- Adapter owns Assessment construction using domain-specific identity, provenance and time context.
- Core owns normative semantic validation.
- Core validation MUST be enforced on every supported registration path.
- A standalone validator that callers can bypass is insufficient.
- An old public registration API MUST NOT remain a validation bypass.
- Publication and retention remain separate responsibilities and must be explicitly assigned by the relevant boundary.
- Downstream consumption does not automatically accept the Assessment as truth or grant authority.

**Scope of approval:** DEC-02 assigns adapter **construction**, Core **semantic validation**, and Core-owned **admission** with an **immutable registered representation**. The adapter constructs candidates and initiates admission through the Core API; it must not mutate admitted state. Persistent storage is **caller-managed**. Publication and retention remain **OPEN**. This paragraph is the canonical scope statement; other documents should reference it rather than paraphrase.

### Validation enforcement

Mandatory Core validation at the registration boundary is approved. The implementation design may choose between validation inside `registerAssessment` or a guarded validated-registration API, provided the old public API cannot bypass validation. No further implementation detail is approved by this decision.

### T18-DEC-15 — parent coverage semantics (OPEN)

CORE-001 does not state whether `ContinuityAssessment.parent_version_ids` must equal the full declared parent set for `(subject_version_id, declared_relation)` or may be the subset covered by the Assessment.

T18-02A uses **Option B** — one Assessment per `(child, relation)`, with the complete declared parent set and at least one parent absent from the local graph — as a **local implementation choice/disposition**. This is not a resolution of the normative question. The question remains OPEN and requires a separate `T18-SPEC-01` clarification before either model is described as normative.

The `Resolution` column is the register's generic field name. For `T18-DEC-15` it records a non-normative local disposition, not a normative resolution.

### Still open

- C-2 Assessment subject model: SCC, node, or edge. Edge-level is a proposal only.
- Exact Assessment data shape and provenance contract.
- Persistent storage, publication and retention ownership.
- C-2 `CYCLE_DETECTED` admission policy (T18-02B; not part of T18-02A).
- Parent-coverage semantics (`T18-DEC-15`).
- C-2.a3 grant suppression and other cross-specification decisions, including CORE-003.

### Path correction

`VAL-CORE-CONSTRUCTION` is only compatible with `OWN-CORE`. It is not a valid option under `OWN-ADAPTER`. The selected path is `OWN-ADAPTER` + `VAL-CORE`.

Task 17 ambiguity identifiers are preserved exactly. They are not renamed and not re-scoped.
